column1: # denylist.tsv -- the rule table behind guard_path().
#   kind      DENY | ASK | ALLOW | CHILDREN | DENYGLOB | ASKGLOB
#   pattern   absolute path, or ~ for $HOME. DENYGLOB/ASKGLOB use shell case globbing.
#   mindepth  minimum path depth (number of '/' separators) required to match
#   mode      self | children | none   (children = delete contents, keep the directory)
#   reason    shown to the user verbatim when the rule fires
#   - DENY/ASK/ALLOW/CHILDREN are PREFIX rules: match if path == pattern or path starts with pattern/
#   - Longest matching pattern wins. Ties break toward the stronger verdict:
#   - A path matching NO rule is DENIED. Default-deny is the whole point.
#   - ~/.clean-mac-ai/denylist.local.tsv is appended after this file but may only
#     STRENGTHEN rules; ALLOW lines there are ignored so nobody can unprotect /System.

column1: # The package-manager prefixes, all three, denied by name.
# These are LIVE installations -- Cellar, Homebrew/Library, opt, bin, lib -- not
# caches. `brew cleanup` is the only collector permitted to touch them, for the
# same reason as Homebrew/brew#5083: the tool understands its own layout and a
# /usr/local is denied explicitly rather than left to fall through to the /usr
# rule above, so the verdict AND the stated reason are identical on Intel and
# Apple Silicon. Before this, `ALLOW /usr/local` meant the entire live Homebrew
# install was ALLOW with needs=none on Intel, while the same install at
# /opt/homebrew was default-denied on Apple Silicon -- default-deny, the core
# safety property, varied with the chip. Homebrew chowns these directories to
# the invoking user, so the root-ownership ASK never fires, and the sunlnk flag
# on /usr/local only protects its direct children.
# At lengths 10, 13 and 10 these also beat the length-0 name rules, so
# node_modules can no longer tunnel into any of the three prefixes.

column1: # ------------------------------------- project build output, wherever it lives
# Unambiguous names only. These are pure derived output: regenerated from source
# by the project's own build system, with no network and no lockfile needed.
# A name rule carries length 0 and so can never override a deny.
# Two names are deliberately NOT here and must never be added:
#   Library -- `ALLOWNAME Library` resolves $HOME/Library to ALLOW, because no
#              DENY prefix covers it and length 0 beats deny_len -1. Verified.
#   bin     -- holds hand-written scripts in a large fraction of repositories.
# tests/lint.sh gate 8b rejects both, and any other reserved directory name.
